# Wireshark Packet Capture and Analysis

## Objective

The objective of this lab is to learn how to capture and analyze network traffic using Wireshark.

This lab focuses on observing:

* ARP communication
* ICMP traffic generated by ping
* Packet details at different network layers

## Lab Environment

| Machine       | Operating System | Role                        |
| ------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| Kali Linux VM | Linux            | Packet capture and analysis |
| Windows VM    | Windows          | Target machine              |

Both machines were connected to the same internal network.

## Tool Used

* Wireshark

## Capture Process

### 0. Clear ARP cache

The ARP cache was cleared to force a new ARP resolution process.

<img width="231" height="91" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6285c967-1c5a-4ea5-a493-a8534296bf05" />

### 1. Started Packet Capture

Opened Wireshark and selected the active network interface.

The capture was started before generating any network traffic.

### 2. Generated Network Traffic

Ping was used to create ICMP traffic:

<img width="505" height="177" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8188b6e0-860c-4e4b-bbdb-703ad906c14f" />

## Packet Analysis

<img width="1267" height="127" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81a09d8b-dcf3-48cb-b26c-a59714c64655" />

Packet 1 — 192.168.56.10 broadcasts an ARP request: "Who has 192.168.56.20? Tell 192.168.56.10." This host wants to ping .20 but doesn't know its MAC address yet, so it asks everyone on the LAN.
Packet 2 — 192.168.56.20 replies directly (ARP reply): "192.168.56.20 is at 08:00:27:ca:0a:04." Now .10 has the MAC it needs.
Packet 3 — 192.168.56.10 sends an ICMP Echo (ping) request to 192.168.56.20, id=0x4bcc, seq=1/256, ttl=64. This is the first ping.
Packet 4 — 192.168.56.20 replies with ICMP Echo reply, same id, seq=1/256, ttl=128. Confirms .20 is reachable.

## Skills Practiced

* Using Wireshark for packet analysis
* Understanding ARP protocol
* Understanding ICMP communication
